questions.prompt: What does an azimuth bearing measure on a map?
options: Direction clockwise from north in degrees
Height above sea level in metres
Distance between two contour lines
Area covered by one grid square
questions.correctAnswer: Direction clockwise from north in degrees
questions.explanation: An azimuth bearing states direction as an angle measured clockwise from north, from 000 degrees to 360 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: State how true bearings are measured and expressed on maps.

questions.prompt: What is the contour interval of a topographical map?
options: The vertical difference in height between adjacent contour lines
The ground distance represented by one centimetre on the map
The direction from one feature to another
The total population shown by a settlement symbol
questions.correctAnswer: The vertical difference in height between adjacent contour lines
questions.explanation: Contour interval is the constant change in elevation between neighbouring contour lines on a map.
questions.learningOutcome: Define key terms used in contour map interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a Geographic Information System?
options: A computer-based system for capturing, analysing and displaying spatial data
A hand lens used to identify minerals in a rock sample
A rainfall gauge installed at a weather station
A written list of historical events arranged by date
questions.correctAnswer: A computer-based system for capturing, analysing and displaying spatial data
questions.explanation: GIS links data to location, allowing learners and planners to map, query, analyse and display spatial patterns.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the basic purpose of GIS in geographical studies.

questions.prompt: What is remote sensing in Geography?
options: Collecting information about the earth from sensors not in direct contact with the surface
Measuring rainfall by emptying a rain gauge each morning
Interviewing residents during a fieldwork survey
Drawing a sketch map from direct ground observation only
questions.correctAnswer: Collecting information about the earth from sensors not in direct contact with the surface
questions.explanation: Remote sensing uses aircraft, satellites or drones to gather information from a distance.
questions.learningOutcome: Define remote sensing as a source of geographical data.

questions.prompt: Which side of a highland usually receives heavier relief rainfall?
options: Windward side
Leeward side
Rain-shadow side only
Side facing away from moist winds
questions.correctAnswer: Windward side
questions.explanation: Moist air is forced to rise on the windward slope, cools, condenses and produces rainfall.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the side of a highland that receives more relief rainfall.

questions.prompt: Which tectonic setting best explains the formation of the East African Rift Valley?
options: Tensional forces pulling the crust apart
Compression forming only fold mountains
Sediment deposition by a mature river
Wave erosion along a rocky coast
questions.correctAnswer: Tensional forces pulling the crust apart
questions.explanation: The rift is associated with crustal stretching, normal faulting and subsidence of blocks between faults.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the crustal forces associated with rift valley formation.

questions.prompt: Karst caves commonly form through which process?
options: Carbonation dissolving limestone
Wind piling sand into dunes
Glacial plucking of hard rock
Cooling of lava on a volcano
questions.correctAnswer: Carbonation dissolving limestone
questions.explanation: Weak carbonic acid in water dissolves limestone along joints and bedding planes, forming underground cavities.
questions.learningOutcome: State the main chemical weathering process responsible for karst cave formation.

questions.prompt: Which landform is produced when a stream deposits sediment where it leaves a steep slope and enters flatter land?
options: Alluvial fan
Stack
Corrie
Volcanic plug
questions.correctAnswer: Alluvial fan
questions.explanation: As a stream loses velocity at the foot of a slope, it deposits its load in a fan-shaped spread.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify depositional landforms formed by streams at slope breaks.

questions.prompt: What is the dew point?
options: The temperature at which air becomes saturated and condensation begins
The highest temperature recorded in a day
The speed at which wind changes direction
The depth of water in a river channel
questions.correctAnswer: The temperature at which air becomes saturated and condensation begins
questions.explanation: At dew point, air holds as much water vapour as it can at that temperature, so condensation can occur.
questions.learningOutcome: Define dew point in relation to condensation.

questions.prompt: What is urbanisation?
options: The growth in the proportion of people living in towns and cities
The movement of soil down a steep slope
The seasonal rise and fall of lake levels
The conversion of minerals into manufactured goods
questions.correctAnswer: The growth in the proportion of people living in towns and cities
questions.explanation: Urbanisation describes the increasing share of a population living in urban settlements.
questions.learningOutcome: Define urbanisation as a population and settlement process.

questions.prompt: Which urban zone usually has the highest concentration of offices, shops and transport terminals?
options: Central business district
Green belt forest
Subsistence farming zone
Remote grazing reserve
questions.correctAnswer: Central business district
questions.explanation: The central business district is the commercial and administrative core of many towns and cities.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major functional zones within urban settlements.

questions.prompt: Which Kenyan region is especially associated with geothermal energy development?
options: The Rift Valley around Olkaria and nearby fields
The coral reefs of the Indian Ocean only
The Yala swamp lowlands only
The top of every coastal sand dune
questions.correctAnswer: The Rift Valley around Olkaria and nearby fields
questions.explanation: Kenya's geothermal potential is linked to volcanic and faulted zones of the Rift Valley, including Olkaria.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify Kenyan examples of geothermal energy resources.

questions.prompt: Which resource is renewable when managed sustainably?
options: Forest trees
Petroleum
Coal seams
Metallic ore bodies
questions.correctAnswer: Forest trees
questions.explanation: Forests can regenerate through natural growth or planting if harvesting does not exceed replacement.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish renewable resources from non-renewable resources.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of an environmental impact assessment before a major project?
options: To predict likely environmental effects and plan mitigation measures
To replace all community consultation with a map title
To guarantee that a project has no cost
To decide the colour of buildings only
questions.correctAnswer: To predict likely environmental effects and plan mitigation measures
questions.explanation: An environmental impact assessment helps decision makers identify risks, compare alternatives and reduce harm before work begins.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of environmental impact assessment in development planning.

questions.prompt: What does desertification mean?
options: Land degradation in dry areas that reduces biological productivity
The daily formation of dew on grass surfaces
The cooling of lava into basalt
The movement of waves along a coastline
questions.correctAnswer: Land degradation in dry areas that reduces biological productivity
questions.explanation: Desertification occurs when dryland ecosystems lose productive soil, vegetation or water capacity through natural and human pressures.
questions.learningOutcome: Define desertification and its effect on dryland productivity.

questions.prompt: On a map with a scale of 1:25,000, what ground distance is represented by 4 cm?
options: 1 km
4 km
10 km
questions.correctAnswer: 1 km
questions.explanation: At 1:25,000, 1 cm represents 250 m, so 4 cm represents 1,000 m or 1 km.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate ground distance from a representative fraction scale.

questions.prompt: A road rises from 900 m to 1200 m over a horizontal ground distance of 3 km. What is its average gradient?
questions.explanation: The rise is 300 m and the horizontal distance is 3,000 m, giving a gradient of 300:3000, simplified to 1:10.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate average gradient using height difference and horizontal distance.

questions.prompt: A feature lies four tenths across from easting 23 and seven tenths up from northing 64. Which six-figure grid reference is correct?
questions.explanation: Six-figure references give the easting first, then the northing: 23 plus 4 tenths becomes 234, and 64 plus 7 tenths becomes 647.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct six-figure grid references from eastings and northings.

questions.prompt: On a contour map, V-shaped contours crossing a river point upstream. If the V shapes point north, which way is the river flowing?
options: South
North
East
West
questions.correctAnswer: South
questions.explanation: Because the contour V points upstream, the river flows in the opposite direction, from north toward south.
questions.learningOutcome: Use contour patterns to infer river flow direction.

questions.prompt: Which sampling approach is most suitable for recording land-use change along a straight line from a city centre to the outskirts?
options: Transect sampling
Snowball sampling
Random guessing
Single household interview only
questions.correctAnswer: Transect sampling
questions.explanation: A transect records observations at intervals along a line, making it useful for studying gradients from urban core to edge.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate sampling methods for geographical field investigations.

questions.prompt: Why does condensation occur when saturated air is cooled?
options: Cooler air can hold less water vapour, so excess vapour changes to droplets
Cooling turns all oxygen into wind
Cold air always becomes completely dry without clouds
Cooling increases the sun's direct radiation
questions.correctAnswer: Cooler air can hold less water vapour, so excess vapour changes to droplets
questions.explanation: When air temperature falls to the dew point, some water vapour condenses into liquid droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between cooling, saturation and condensation.

questions.prompt: A station at 500 m records 27 degrees C. Using a lapse rate of 6.5 degrees C per 1000 m, what is the estimated temperature at 1500 m?
options: About 20.5 degrees C
About 26.5 degrees C
About 33.5 degrees C
About 6.5 degrees C
questions.correctAnswer: About 20.5 degrees C
questions.explanation: The second station is 1,000 m higher, so temperature is estimated to fall by 6.5 degrees C from 27 degrees C.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply environmental lapse rate to estimate temperature with altitude.

questions.prompt: Why is the leeward side of a mountain often drier than the windward side?
options: Air descending the leeward slope warms and becomes less likely to condense
The leeward side always receives ocean currents directly
Mountains create rainfall only at night
Descending air automatically turns into river water
questions.correctAnswer: Air descending the leeward slope warms and becomes less likely to condense
questions.explanation: After losing moisture on the windward side, air descends, warms and forms a rain-shadow effect on the leeward side.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why relief can create wet and dry zones around highlands.

questions.prompt: Why is convectional rainfall common around warm lake and equatorial areas during afternoon hours?
options: Strong surface heating makes moist air rise, cool and condense
Cold ocean currents freeze all clouds near the surface
Dry descending air prevents all uplift
High pressure forces rain to fall without cloud formation
questions.correctAnswer: Strong surface heating makes moist air rise, cool and condense
questions.explanation: Convectional rainfall develops when heated moist air rises rapidly and forms cumulonimbus clouds.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the process leading to convectional rainfall.

questions.prompt: What does a soil catena show?
options: A sequence of related soils down a slope
A list of weather instruments in a station
A chain of towns in a transport corridor
A set of waves approaching a coastline
questions.correctAnswer: A sequence of related soils down a slope
questions.explanation: A catena shows how soils vary from hilltop to valley floor because of drainage, erosion, deposition and slope position.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how relief influences soil variation along a slope.

questions.prompt: Which process is most associated with laterite formation in humid tropical regions?
options: Intense leaching leaving iron and aluminium oxides
Glacial deposition of moraine ridges
Wind sorting of sand into dunes
Wave refraction around headlands
questions.correctAnswer: Intense leaching leaving iron and aluminium oxides
questions.explanation: Heavy rainfall leaches soluble minerals from tropical soils, often concentrating iron and aluminium compounds.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate tropical climate and leaching to lateritic soil formation.

questions.prompt: A river channel has many shifting bars and several shallow interlacing channels. Which condition is most likely?
options: Variable discharge with a heavy coarse sediment load
A perfectly constant discharge with no sediment
Permanent deep water and no deposition
Only underground flow through limestone
questions.correctAnswer: Variable discharge with a heavy coarse sediment load
questions.explanation: Braided channels form where rivers carry more sediment than they can transport steadily, especially with fluctuating flow.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain conditions that favour braided river channels.

questions.prompt: Why does a delta form at some river mouths?
options: The river loses energy and deposits sediment faster than waves and currents remove it
The river suddenly increases its gradient at the sea
Ocean waves carry all sediment back upstream
The river mouth becomes too steep for deposition
questions.correctAnswer: The river loses energy and deposits sediment faster than waves and currents remove it
questions.explanation: Deltas grow where deposition at a low-energy river mouth exceeds removal by marine processes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the formation of deltas at river mouths.

questions.prompt: What is one effect of wave refraction on an irregular coastline?
options: Wave energy is concentrated on headlands and spread out in bays
All beaches become equally steep at once
Rivers stop flowing into the sea
Coastal winds stop moving sediment
questions.correctAnswer: Wave energy is concentrated on headlands and spread out in bays
questions.explanation: Refraction bends waves so erosion is stronger on headlands while deposition is favoured in sheltered bays.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how wave refraction influences erosion and deposition on coasts.

questions.prompt: Which adaptation helps mangrove trees survive in waterlogged tidal mud?
options: Breathing roots that rise above the mud surface
Deep taproots that avoid all salt water
Needles that store snow during winter
Wide leaves that stop all transpiration permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Breathing roots that rise above the mud surface
questions.explanation: Many mangroves have pneumatophores or aerial roots that improve gas exchange in oxygen-poor mud.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe plant adaptations in mangrove environments.

questions.prompt: What population change is likely when birth rates remain high while death rates fall quickly?
options: Rapid natural increase
Immediate population decline
No change in total population
Only international migration
questions.correctAnswer: Rapid natural increase
questions.explanation: Natural increase rises when births greatly exceed deaths, especially after improvements in health and sanitation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how birth and death rates affect population growth.

questions.prompt: What does a high dependency ratio indicate?
options: Many young and elderly people compared with the working-age population
Many exports compared with imports
Many rivers compared with roads
Many factories compared with farms
questions.correctAnswer: Many young and elderly people compared with the working-age population
questions.explanation: Dependency ratio compares dependants with the economically active age group, showing pressure on workers and services.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret dependency ratio as a population planning indicator.

questions.prompt: Which factor is a common pull factor for rural-urban migration?
options: Expectation of employment, education and health services in towns
Loss of crops due to drought in the village
Land fragmentation in a rural home area
Declining pasture in a dry-season grazing zone
questions.correctAnswer: Expectation of employment, education and health services in towns
questions.explanation: Pull factors attract migrants to a destination, while push factors drive them away from the origin area.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish pull factors from push factors in migration decisions.

questions.prompt: Which settlement pattern is most likely to develop along a road, river or coastline?
options: Linear settlement
Dispersed settlement
Radial drainage settlement
Random volcanic settlement
questions.correctAnswer: Linear settlement
questions.explanation: Linear settlements grow in a line along transport routes, rivers, coasts or valley floors.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate settlement patterns to physical and transport features.

questions.prompt: Why are tea-growing areas in Kenya often found in humid highland zones?
options: Tea grows well in cool temperatures, reliable rainfall and well-drained acidic soils
Tea requires hot desert conditions and saline soils
Tea can only grow below sea level
Tea farming depends mainly on ocean waves
questions.correctAnswer: Tea grows well in cool temperatures, reliable rainfall and well-drained acidic soils
questions.explanation: Kenyan tea is favoured by highland climates with adequate rainfall and suitable soils.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain physical factors influencing crop distribution in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why are sugar factories commonly located near cane-growing areas?
options: Sugarcane is bulky and loses sucrose after harvesting
Sugarcane becomes lighter after long storage
Factories do not need transport links
Sugarcane grows only inside factory buildings
questions.correctAnswer: Sugarcane is bulky and loses sucrose after harvesting
questions.explanation: Processing near farms reduces transport cost and quality loss for a bulky, perishable raw material.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain raw-material influence on agro-processing industries.

questions.prompt: What does the tourism multiplier effect describe?
options: How tourist spending creates further income and jobs in related sectors
How all tourists visit the same site twice
How rainfall doubles when visitors arrive
How a hotel replaces every other economic activity
questions.correctAnswer: How tourist spending creates further income and jobs in related sectors
questions.explanation: Tourist spending can support transport, food supply, guiding, crafts and other local businesses beyond the first purchase.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how tourism can affect local economies.

questions.prompt: How does containerisation improve international transport?
options: It standardises cargo handling between ships, rail and trucks
It removes the need for ports and roads
It makes all goods weightless
It prevents any customs documentation
questions.correctAnswer: It standardises cargo handling between ships, rail and trucks
questions.explanation: Containers reduce handling time, improve security and make transfers between transport modes easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of containerisation in modern transport systems.

questions.prompt: What is aquifer recharge?
options: The addition of water to underground water-bearing rocks
The removal of all water from a lake
The cooling of magma below a volcano
The cutting of timber from a forest
questions.correctAnswer: The addition of water to underground water-bearing rocks
questions.explanation: Recharge happens when water infiltrates and percolates into permeable rocks or sediments that store groundwater.
questions.learningOutcome: Define aquifer recharge as part of groundwater management.

questions.prompt: Which waste management sequence best follows the waste hierarchy?
options: Reduce waste, reuse materials, recycle, then safely dispose of residues
Burn all waste first, then sort ashes later
Dispose first and think about recycling afterwards
Mix hazardous and organic waste to save space
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce waste, reuse materials, recycle, then safely dispose of residues
questions.explanation: The hierarchy gives priority to preventing waste and recovering value before final disposal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the waste hierarchy to urban environmental management.

questions.prompt: If it is 3:00 p.m. at longitude 45 degrees E, what is the local time at longitude 30 degrees E?
questions.explanation: The difference is 15 degrees of longitude, equal to one hour. Places to the west are earlier in local time.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate local time differences using longitude.

questions.prompt: A rectangular forest measures 3 cm by 2 cm on a 1:50,000 map. What is its approximate ground area?
options: 1.5 square kilometres
5 square kilometres
15 square kilometres
0.15 square kilometres
questions.correctAnswer: 1.5 square kilometres
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm is 0.5 km, so the rectangle is 1.5 km by 1.0 km, giving 1.5 square kilometres.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate ground area from map dimensions and scale.

questions.prompt: A cross-section uses a horizontal scale of 1 cm to 500 m and a vertical scale of 1 cm to 100 m. What is the vertical exaggeration?
options: 5 times
2 times
50 times
0.5 times
questions.correctAnswer: 5 times
questions.explanation: Vertical exaggeration compares the horizontal scale unit with the vertical scale unit: 500 m divided by 100 m equals 5.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate vertical exaggeration for geographical cross-sections.

questions.prompt: A map description says a river channel is dry for much of the year and flows mainly after heavy rain. Which term best fits it?
options: Seasonal stream
Permanent river
Ocean current
Artificial contour
questions.correctAnswer: Seasonal stream
questions.explanation: A seasonal or intermittent stream flows only during wet periods or after storms, especially in dry regions.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret drainage descriptions from map and field evidence.

questions.prompt: A fieldwork team wants reliable information on how a market centre affects nearby traffic and land use. Which method combination is strongest?
options: Traffic counts, land-use mapping, interviews and repeated observations at set times
One informal guess made from a classroom desk
Only counting vehicles during a power blackout
Copying results from a different town without checking
questions.correctAnswer: Traffic counts, land-use mapping, interviews and repeated observations at set times
questions.explanation: Combining direct measurement, mapping and interviews improves reliability and gives both quantitative and qualitative evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Select complementary methods for urban field investigations.

questions.prompt: Which GIS operation would identify all schools within 500 m of a busy highway?
options: Buffer analysis
Weather balloon launch
Rock hardness test
Random deletion of map layers
questions.correctAnswer: Buffer analysis
questions.explanation: A buffer creates a zone around a feature, allowing features within a specified distance to be selected.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply GIS operations to answer spatial planning questions.

questions.prompt: Why can satellite images help monitor forest cover change over time?
options: Images taken at different dates can be compared to detect loss or regrowth
Satellites replace all need for location data
Satellite images show only underground minerals
Images from space cannot record vegetation patterns
questions.correctAnswer: Images taken at different dates can be compared to detect loss or regrowth
questions.explanation: Remote sensing supports change detection by comparing repeated observations of the same area.
questions.learningOutcome: Use remote sensing reasoning to monitor environmental change.

questions.prompt: How does the seasonal movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone affect East African rainfall?
options: It shifts zones of rising moist air, influencing the timing of rainy seasons
It permanently blocks all rainfall from the equator
It creates snowfall at sea level throughout the year
It stops monsoon winds from changing direction
questions.correctAnswer: It shifts zones of rising moist air, influencing the timing of rainy seasons
questions.explanation: The ITCZ is a belt of converging trade winds and uplift that migrates seasonally, helping shape rainfall seasons.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how global pressure belts influence East African rainfall seasons.

questions.prompt: A station has mean monthly temperatures above 24 degrees C and annual rainfall below 300 mm. Which climate description best fits it?
options: Hot arid climate
Cool temperate climate
Humid equatorial climate
Alpine climate
questions.correctAnswer: Hot arid climate
questions.explanation: High temperatures and very low rainfall indicate hot arid conditions rather than humid or highland climates.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify climate from simple temperature and rainfall data.

questions.prompt: Why do cloudy nights usually have a smaller fall in temperature than clear nights?
options: Clouds absorb and re-radiate some outgoing longwave radiation
Clouds make the sun shine at night
Clouds remove all water vapour from the air
Clouds increase the earth's distance from the sun
questions.correctAnswer: Clouds absorb and re-radiate some outgoing longwave radiation
questions.explanation: Cloud cover reduces night-time heat loss from the surface, keeping minimum temperatures higher.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how cloud cover affects diurnal temperature range.

questions.prompt: During some El Nino episodes, many parts of East Africa experience unusually heavy rainfall. Which hazard becomes more likely?
options: Flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas
Complete absence of river flow everywhere
Permanent disappearance of humidity
Formation of glaciers on all hills
questions.correctAnswer: Flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas
questions.explanation: Above-normal rainfall can saturate slopes, raise river levels and increase flood or landslide risk where exposure is high.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate climate variability to weather-related hazards in East Africa.

questions.prompt: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole often warms the western Indian Ocean relative to the east. How can this affect East Africa?
options: It can strengthen moisture inflow and increase rainfall chances in parts of the region
It always stops all cloud formation over land
It turns trade winds into ocean waves only
It has no possible link to regional rainfall
questions.correctAnswer: It can strengthen moisture inflow and increase rainfall chances in parts of the region
questions.explanation: Warmer western Indian Ocean waters can enhance evaporation and moisture transport toward East Africa during some seasons.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how ocean temperature patterns may influence regional rainfall.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best describes rift valley formation by faulting?
options: Tension stretches the crust, parallel normal faults form, and the central block subsides
Compression folds all rocks upward into one dome
Waves erode a headland until a stack remains
A river deposits silt across a floodplain
questions.correctAnswer: Tension stretches the crust, parallel normal faults form, and the central block subsides
questions.explanation: A rift valley develops where extensional forces produce normal faults and downthrow between raised blocks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the sequence of processes that forms a rift valley.

questions.prompt: How does a volcanic plug become exposed as a landform?
options: Softer surrounding rock is eroded, leaving hardened magma in the vent standing out
Fresh lava is deposited evenly across a floodplain
A glacier melts and drops clay in a lake
Wind removes salt from ocean water
questions.correctAnswer: Softer surrounding rock is eroded, leaving hardened magma in the vent standing out
questions.explanation: A plug is resistant solidified magma within a vent; erosion can remove weaker surrounding material and expose it.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how erosion can expose intrusive volcanic features.

questions.prompt: In a dry landscape, why might an inselberg remain standing above a plain?
options: It is made of more resistant rock than the surrounding weathered material
It is composed only of loose river silt
It is lower than all nearby surfaces
It is created by coral growth in deep ocean water
questions.correctAnswer: It is made of more resistant rock than the surrounding weathered material
questions.explanation: Differential weathering and erosion remove weaker rocks faster, leaving resistant residual hills such as inselbergs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the formation of residual landforms in dry environments.

questions.prompt: Which feature is typical of a cuesta landscape?
options: A gentle dip slope and a steep scarp slope
A circular coral reef around a lagoon
A deep glacial corrie filled with ice
A flat delta with distributaries only
questions.correctAnswer: A gentle dip slope and a steep scarp slope
questions.explanation: Cuestas form in gently dipping strata where resistant rock creates an asymmetrical ridge.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify landforms controlled by rock structure and dip.

questions.prompt: Which evidence suggests that a river has been rejuvenated?
options: River terraces and a knickpoint along the valley
Only a smooth delta at sea level
No change in valley gradient anywhere
A desert sand dune beside the channel
questions.correctAnswer: River terraces and a knickpoint along the valley
questions.explanation: Rejuvenation renews a river's erosive power, often producing knickpoints, incised meanders and terraces.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify landform evidence of renewed river erosion.

questions.prompt: Which field evidence most clearly indicates active soil erosion on a cultivated slope?
options: Rills, exposed roots and sediment deposited at the foot of the slope
Uniform crop cover and stable grass strips
Deep litter cover and clear infiltration basins
No runoff marks after heavy rain
questions.correctAnswer: Rills, exposed roots and sediment deposited at the foot of the slope
questions.explanation: Small channels, exposed roots and downslope sediment show that runoff is removing soil from the slope.
questions.learningOutcome: Use field evidence to identify active soil erosion.

questions.prompt: A bare lava surface is gradually colonised by lichens, grasses, shrubs and then trees. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Primary succession
Urban sprawl
Longshore drift
Population census
questions.correctAnswer: Primary succession
questions.explanation: Primary succession begins on a surface with little or no soil and develops through stages as organisms build soil and habitat.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ecological succession on newly exposed surfaces.

questions.prompt: Why can shallow wells near poorly sited pit latrines become unsafe?
options: Pathogens and nitrates can percolate into groundwater
Latrines automatically purify aquifers
Groundwater cannot move through soil or rock
Shallow wells contain only rainbows and air
questions.correctAnswer: Pathogens and nitrates can percolate into groundwater
questions.explanation: Contaminants can move downward with infiltrating water, especially where wells are shallow or soils are highly permeable.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse local factors that can contaminate groundwater sources.

questions.prompt: In the demographic transition model, which situation produces the fastest natural population growth?
options: Death rates have fallen but birth rates remain high
Birth rates and death rates are both very high
Birth rates are lower than death rates
Birth rates and death rates are both near zero
questions.correctAnswer: Death rates have fallen but birth rates remain high
questions.explanation: Rapid growth occurs when mortality declines before fertility falls, widening the gap between births and deaths.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the demographic transition model to explain population growth patterns.

questions.prompt: A population pyramid has a very wide base and narrows quickly with age. What does this suggest?
options: A youthful population with high birth rates
An ageing population with very low fertility
A population with no children
A settlement pattern controlled by roads only
questions.correctAnswer: A youthful population with high birth rates
questions.explanation: A wide base shows many young people, usually linked to high fertility and strong demand for schools and child services.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret population pyramids for planning needs.

questions.prompt: Which combination best explains rural-urban migration from a dry rural area to a large town?
options: Drought and limited rural jobs push people while urban employment and services attract them
High crop yields push people from town to rural farms only
Reliable pasture and water push people away from towns
Urban areas attract migrants because they lack services
questions.correctAnswer: Drought and limited rural jobs push people while urban employment and services attract them
questions.explanation: Migration decisions often combine push factors at the origin with pull factors at the destination.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse push and pull factors in internal migration.

questions.prompt: A small town grows rapidly after a new university, hospital and bus terminal are built. Which process is most likely occurring?
options: Growth of service functions increasing the town's centrality
Formation of a volcanic cone by eruption
Reduction of all transport links
Conversion of urban land into permanent ice
questions.correctAnswer: Growth of service functions increasing the town's centrality
questions.explanation: Higher-order services attract users from a wider area and can strengthen a town's role as a central place.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how services influence growth and hierarchy of settlements.

questions.prompt: Why do built-up urban areas often have higher night temperatures than nearby rural areas?
options: Concrete and asphalt store heat and release it slowly after sunset
Cities always receive more direct sunlight at night
Rural areas contain no air or water vapour
Urban buildings stop all longwave radiation from existing
questions.correctAnswer: Concrete and asphalt store heat and release it slowly after sunset
questions.explanation: Urban heat islands develop from heat-absorbing surfaces, reduced vegetation, waste heat and altered airflow.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain causes of the urban heat island effect.

questions.prompt: Which factor can contribute to the growth of informal settlements in fast-growing cities?
options: Rapid migration combined with limited affordable housing and serviced land
Excess empty high-quality housing for all residents
Complete absence of employment opportunities in every city
Permanent ban on all rural-urban movement
questions.correctAnswer: Rapid migration combined with limited affordable housing and serviced land
questions.explanation: When urban population grows faster than formal housing supply and infrastructure, informal settlements may expand.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse causes of informal settlement growth in urban areas.

questions.prompt: Why are specialist hospitals usually found in larger urban centres rather than every small village?
options: They require a large threshold population and wider market range
They need to be far from all patients
They operate only where there are no roads
They depend mainly on fertile volcanic soils
questions.correctAnswer: They require a large threshold population and wider market range
questions.explanation: High-order services need enough users and purchasing power, so they are concentrated in larger central places.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply threshold and range concepts to service distribution.

questions.prompt: In a land-use model around a city, why are vegetables and milk production often located close to the urban market?
options: They are perishable and benefit from short transport time
They are always mined from deep shafts
They need to be transported for many years before sale
They require no consumers
questions.correctAnswer: They are perishable and benefit from short transport time
questions.explanation: Perishable and high-value products are often produced near markets to reduce spoilage and transport cost.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply market-distance reasoning to agricultural land use.

questions.prompt: Which problem may develop in an irrigation scheme if drainage is poor in a hot dry area?
options: Waterlogging and soil salinisation
Permanent removal of all soil minerals
Instant formation of glaciers
Complete disappearance of evaporation
questions.correctAnswer: Waterlogging and soil salinisation
questions.explanation: Poor drainage raises the water table, and evaporation can leave salts near the surface in dry climates.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain environmental risks associated with poorly drained irrigation schemes.

questions.prompt: Why can industries benefit from clustering in one industrial area?
options: They can share labour, services, suppliers, infrastructure and markets
They become isolated from all transport routes
They no longer need raw materials or energy
They stop producing waste automatically
questions.correctAnswer: They can share labour, services, suppliers, infrastructure and markets
questions.explanation: Industrial agglomeration can reduce costs and improve efficiency through shared advantages and linkages.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain advantages of industrial clustering.

questions.prompt: Why is geothermal power promising in Kenya's Rift Valley but still costly to expand?
options: Heat sources are favourable, but exploration drilling and steam-field development require high capital
The Rift Valley has no volcanic heat and no faults
Geothermal plants use only imported rainfall
Steam wells can be drilled without technical risk or cost
questions.correctAnswer: Heat sources are favourable, but exploration drilling and steam-field development require high capital
questions.explanation: Geothermal potential is strong in tectonically active zones, but finding and developing productive reservoirs is expensive and technically demanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse opportunities and constraints in geothermal energy development.

questions.prompt: A dry county has high sunshine, scarce river flow and dispersed settlements. Which energy option is most suitable for many local services?
options: Decentralised solar systems with storage and maintenance support
Large hydropower plants on non-existent permanent rivers
Expanded charcoal burning without tree replacement
Diesel generators only with no fuel supply plan
questions.correctAnswer: Decentralised solar systems with storage and maintenance support
questions.explanation: Solar systems match high insolation and dispersed demand better than water-dependent generation in many arid areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate energy options using local physical and settlement conditions.

questions.prompt: Fertiliser runoff enters a lake and causes rapid algal growth followed by fish deaths. Which process best explains this?
options: Eutrophication reducing dissolved oxygen after algal decay
Wave refraction increasing beach deposition
Thermal inversion creating a mountain breeze
Carbonation dissolving limestone cliffs
questions.correctAnswer: Eutrophication reducing dissolved oxygen after algal decay
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment can trigger algal blooms; decomposition uses oxygen, stressing or killing aquatic life.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse causes and effects of nutrient pollution in water bodies.

questions.prompt: Which catchment plan best reduces reservoir siltation downstream?
options: Terracing, riparian buffers, reforestation, controlled grazing and sediment monitoring upstream
Clearing all vegetation on steep slopes
Cultivating river banks to the water edge
Deepening gullies so runoff moves faster
questions.correctAnswer: Terracing, riparian buffers, reforestation, controlled grazing and sediment monitoring upstream
questions.explanation: Siltation is reduced by controlling erosion at source and monitoring sediment movement through the catchment.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate integrated measures for reducing soil erosion and reservoir sedimentation.

questions.prompt: Which strategy best supports drought resilience in a pastoral dryland area?
options: Protect mobility corridors, manage water points, conserve fodder and use early warning information
Fence all grazing routes without alternatives
Increase herd size during drought without feed planning
Locate water points randomly without community rules
questions.correctAnswer: Protect mobility corridors, manage water points, conserve fodder and use early warning information
questions.explanation: Pastoral resilience depends on planned access to pasture and water, risk information and resource governance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse drought-risk reduction strategies for pastoral areas.

questions.prompt: A beach resort area faces erosion and loss of dunes. Which management approach is most sustainable?
options: Maintain dune vegetation, control building setbacks, manage access and monitor shoreline change
Build houses directly on dunes and remove vegetation
Mine beach sand to deepen the shore
Ignore erosion until buildings collapse
questions.correctAnswer: Maintain dune vegetation, control building setbacks, manage access and monitor shoreline change
questions.explanation: Soft engineering and land-use controls protect natural buffers while reducing exposure of people and property.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate sustainable strategies for managing coastal erosion risk.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer imports raw materials and exports finished goods through the Indian Ocean. Which location factor is most important?
options: Access to an efficient port, rail or road corridor
Distance from all transport networks
Location on the steepest mountain summit
Absence of electricity and water supply
questions.correctAnswer: Access to an efficient port, rail or road corridor
questions.explanation: For import-export industries, transport access reduces cost, delays and handling losses.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse transport factors in industrial location decisions.

questions.prompt: Which tourism policy best protects a fragile wildlife area while supporting local livelihoods?
options: Visitor limits, zoning, community revenue sharing and strict waste controls
Unlimited off-road driving in breeding areas
Keeping all income away from nearby communities
Building hotels in every wetland section
questions.correctAnswer: Visitor limits, zoning, community revenue sharing and strict waste controls
questions.explanation: Sustainable tourism balances conservation, visitor experience, local benefits and pollution control.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate tourism management strategies in fragile environments.

questions.prompt: Before mineral sands are mined near a coastal settlement, which requirement is most defensible?
options: Environmental and social assessment with rehabilitation, water and livelihood safeguards
Immediate excavation without baseline studies
Disposal of tailings into fishing grounds
Removal of community access to information
questions.correctAnswer: Environmental and social assessment with rehabilitation, water and livelihood safeguards
questions.explanation: Responsible mining planning should address ecological risks, community impacts, pollution control and post-mining land use.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate responsible mining practices in sensitive environments.

questions.prompt: Which package best supports sustainable fish resources in a lake?
options: Closed seasons, legal mesh sizes, pollution control and community co-management
Use of illegal small-mesh nets throughout the year
Dumping industrial waste to increase nutrients
Removing all breeding grounds for easier boating
questions.correctAnswer: Closed seasons, legal mesh sizes, pollution control and community co-management
questions.explanation: Sustainable fisheries need rules that protect breeding, reduce juvenile catch, control habitat damage and involve users.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse strategies for sustainable use of freshwater fish resources.

questions.prompt: Which transport plan is most likely to reduce congestion and emissions in a large city?
options: Integrated public transport, safe walking and cycling routes, and compact land-use planning
Widening roads while ignoring buses and pedestrians
Removing sidewalks to create more car lanes
Locating housing far from jobs without transit
questions.correctAnswer: Integrated public transport, safe walking and cycling routes, and compact land-use planning
questions.explanation: Efficient urban mobility combines transport modes and land use to reduce long trips and private-car dependence.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse integrated strategies for sustainable urban transport.

questions.prompt: A new highway bypass creates service centres at interchanges outside a town. What geographical effect is most likely?
options: New roadside commercial nodes and outward urban growth
Immediate disappearance of all settlements
Conversion of the highway into a river
End of all commuting and trade
questions.correctAnswer: New roadside commercial nodes and outward urban growth
questions.explanation: Major transport routes can redirect accessibility, encourage businesses near junctions and influence urban expansion.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how transport infrastructure influences settlement patterns.

questions.prompt: A county has a very youthful population structure. Which planning priority is most directly implied?
options: Expanding schools, health services, skills training and future job opportunities
Reducing all investment in education
Building only retirement homes immediately
Ignoring population data until the next century
questions.correctAnswer: Expanding schools, health services, skills training and future job opportunities
questions.explanation: A youthful population creates high demand for child services now and employment preparation for the future workforce.
questions.learningOutcome: Use population structure to infer service and employment planning needs.

questions.prompt: Why can a high-rainfall farming area still experience food insecurity?
options: Land fragmentation, soil exhaustion, pests, poverty or poor market access can limit food availability
High rainfall automatically guarantees surplus food for every household
Food security depends only on annual rainfall totals
Markets and storage have no effect on food supply
questions.correctAnswer: Land fragmentation, soil exhaustion, pests, poverty or poor market access can limit food availability
questions.explanation: Food security depends on production, access, stability and utilisation, not rainfall alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse multiple factors affecting food security in farming regions.

questions.prompt: Which farming adaptation is strongest for a semi-arid area facing more frequent dry spells?
options: Drought-tolerant varieties, water harvesting, mulching, timely planting and diversified livelihoods
Only high-water crops without irrigation
Removing all soil cover before the dry season
Ignoring seasonal forecasts and planting randomly
questions.correctAnswer: Drought-tolerant varieties, water harvesting, mulching, timely planting and diversified livelihoods
questions.explanation: A combined adaptation package reduces exposure to rainfall failure and spreads production risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate farming adaptations to dryland climate risk.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes climate mitigation from adaptation?
options: Mitigation reduces causes of climate change, while adaptation reduces harm from its impacts
Mitigation means moving uphill, while adaptation means moving downhill
Both terms mean exactly the same action in all cases
Adaptation only applies to rocks and never to people
questions.correctAnswer: Mitigation reduces causes of climate change, while adaptation reduces harm from its impacts
questions.explanation: Mitigation targets emissions or carbon sinks, while adaptation adjusts systems to cope with climate-related risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate mitigation and adaptation in climate-risk management.

questions.prompt: Which GIS criteria are most appropriate for selecting a sanitary landfill site?
options: Distance from settlements and water bodies, suitable geology, road access and low flood risk
Closest possible location to wells and schools
Steep unstable slopes with frequent flooding
Only the cheapest land without environmental checks
questions.correctAnswer: Distance from settlements and water bodies, suitable geology, road access and low flood risk
questions.explanation: Landfill siting must reduce pollution and nuisance while remaining accessible for waste collection.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse spatial criteria for environmental planning decisions.

questions.prompt: Why should remote sensing results often be checked with ground observations?
options: Ground truthing verifies image interpretation and reduces classification errors
Ground visits make satellite images unnecessary in every case
Satellites can only photograph underground caves
Ground checks remove all need for coordinates
questions.correctAnswer: Ground truthing verifies image interpretation and reduces classification errors
questions.explanation: Field checks confirm whether mapped features on an image match real conditions on the ground.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate the need for ground truthing in remote sensing studies.

questions.prompt: Which data set is most useful for mapping landslide susceptibility in a highland area?
options: Slope angle, rainfall intensity, geology, soil depth, land cover and past landslide locations
Only names of shops in the nearest town
Ocean tide levels from a coral reef
Number of buses at a flat bus park only
questions.correctAnswer: Slope angle, rainfall intensity, geology, soil depth, land cover and past landslide locations
questions.explanation: Landslide risk depends on terrain, water, materials, vegetation and evidence of previous slope failure.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse physical and land-use factors used in landslide-risk mapping.

questions.prompt: A wetland is proposed for conversion into housing, but nearby residents depend on it for water filtering, grazing and flood storage. Which evaluation is strongest?
options: Compare housing benefits with wetland ecosystem services, legal buffers and livelihood impacts
Approve conversion because wetlands have no economic value
Drain the wetland before identifying users
Ignore flood storage because it is not visible every day
questions.correctAnswer: Compare housing benefits with wetland ecosystem services, legal buffers and livelihood impacts
questions.explanation: Sound land-use decisions weigh development gains against ecological functions, hazards and social dependence.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate trade-offs in wetland conversion and conservation.

questions.prompt: A flood-prone urban river corridor has informal housing, blocked drains and polluted water. Which integrated plan is strongest?
options: Map risk zones, protect riparian reserves, improve drainage, upgrade safe housing and build early warning systems
Clear vegetation, deepen waste channels and allow more building on the river bank
Move all residents without services, mapping or consultation
Wait for the next flood before collecting any data
questions.correctAnswer: Map risk zones, protect riparian reserves, improve drainage, upgrade safe housing and build early warning systems
questions.explanation: Urban flood management needs spatial planning, infrastructure, ecosystem protection, safer settlement and preparedness.
questions.learningOutcome: Design integrated strategies for reducing urban flood risk.

questions.prompt: A class wants to investigate urban heat islands in two neighbourhoods. Which fieldwork design is most reliable?
options: Measure temperature at comparable times, record land cover, repeat readings and map the results
Take one reading at noon in only one street
Ask learners to guess which area is hotter
Use rainfall totals instead of temperature data
questions.correctAnswer: Measure temperature at comparable times, record land cover, repeat readings and map the results
questions.explanation: Reliable microclimate fieldwork controls timing, repeats measurements and links temperature patterns to surface conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a valid field investigation of urban microclimates.

questions.prompt: A county plans a new dryland irrigation scheme. Which feasibility study is most complete?
options: Assess water reliability, soil drainage, crop demand, farmer organisation, costs and downstream impacts
Start construction before checking water availability
Use only one season of crop prices and no soil data
Ignore downstream users because they are outside the scheme
questions.correctAnswer: Assess water reliability, soil drainage, crop demand, farmer organisation, costs and downstream impacts
questions.explanation: Irrigation feasibility must consider physical, economic, institutional and environmental conditions together.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate feasibility criteria for irrigation development in dryland areas.

questions.prompt: Which coastal resilience plan best addresses sea-level rise and storm-surge risk?
options: Setback zones, mangrove restoration, raised infrastructure, evacuation routes and controlled development
Build permanent housing on tidal flats without drainage
Remove mangroves to improve sea views
Ignore storm records because storms are temporary
questions.correctAnswer: Setback zones, mangrove restoration, raised infrastructure, evacuation routes and controlled development
questions.explanation: Coastal resilience combines land-use control, ecosystem buffers, safer infrastructure and emergency planning.
questions.learningOutcome: Create adaptation strategies for coastal hazards and sea-level rise.

questions.prompt: A metropolitan area is expanding into farmland and wetlands. Which planning approach best manages sprawl?
options: Compact mixed-use growth, public transport corridors, protected ecological zones and serviced affordable housing
Allow low-density building everywhere without infrastructure
Fill wetlands first and plan drainage later
Separate housing from all jobs and transit
questions.correctAnswer: Compact mixed-use growth, public transport corridors, protected ecological zones and serviced affordable housing
questions.explanation: Managing sprawl requires coordinated land-use, transport, housing and environmental protection.
questions.learningOutcome: Design sustainable strategies for managing urban expansion.

questions.prompt: Which GIS criteria would best guide emergency water-point placement in an arid pastoral area?
options: Settlement locations, grazing routes, aquifer potential, road access, conflict risk and environmental limits
Random points far from communities and livestock routes
Only the colour of satellite images without field checks
Places selected because they are hardest to reach
questions.correctAnswer: Settlement locations, grazing routes, aquifer potential, road access, conflict risk and environmental limits
questions.explanation: Emergency water planning must be accessible, technically feasible, socially acceptable and environmentally sustainable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply spatial criteria to plan emergency resource access in dryland environments.

questions.prompt: A reforestation carbon project restricts grazing and fuelwood access for nearby households. Which evaluation is most balanced?
options: It may increase carbon storage but must protect community rights, livelihoods and biodiversity
It is automatically fair because all tree planting has no trade-offs
It should ignore residents to store carbon faster
It has no relationship to land use or climate
questions.correctAnswer: It may increase carbon storage but must protect community rights, livelihoods and biodiversity
questions.explanation: Conservation and carbon projects are stronger when climate benefits are matched with social safeguards and ecological quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate social and environmental trade-offs in forest carbon projects.

questions.prompt: A wildlife tourism destination faces drought stress, crowding and community concern over benefits. Which management plan is most coherent?
options: Limit visitor pressure, diversify water management, share revenue locally and monitor ecosystem indicators
Increase vehicle access everywhere during drought
Keep all tourism revenue away from neighbouring communities
Ignore wildlife condition as long as bookings rise
questions.correctAnswer: Limit visitor pressure, diversify water management, share revenue locally and monitor ecosystem indicators
questions.explanation: Resilient tourism planning links ecological limits, climate stress, local benefits and monitoring.
questions.learningOutcome: Design sustainable tourism responses to environmental and social pressures.

questions.prompt: Which national energy strategy best improves reliability while reducing environmental pressure?
options: Diversify geothermal, wind, solar and hydro, improve efficiency, strengthen grids and assess project impacts
Depend on one fuel source and ignore demand growth
Expand charcoal use without forest replacement
Build generation projects without transmission planning
questions.correctAnswer: Diversify geothermal, wind, solar and hydro, improve efficiency, strengthen grids and assess project impacts
questions.explanation: A resilient energy system combines diverse sources, efficient use, grid capacity and environmental safeguards.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate integrated energy strategies for sustainable development.

questions.prompt: A county town wants to reduce open dumping and create local jobs from waste. Which circular-economy plan is strongest?
options: Separate waste at source, compost organics, recycle materials, regulate disposal and support repair or reuse enterprises
Mix all waste and burn it beside homes
Close all collection points without alternatives
Dump waste in wetlands to fill land for buildings
questions.correctAnswer: Separate waste at source, compost organics, recycle materials, regulate disposal and support repair or reuse enterprises
questions.explanation: Circular waste management recovers value, reduces pollution and reserves disposal for residues that cannot be reused or recycled.
questions.learningOutcome: Design integrated solid-waste strategies for urban sustainability.
